t: What Experimental Protocol Library Is All About
title: What Experimental Protocol Library Is All About
description: A protocol is a complete recipe for an experiment: materials, quantities, conditions, steps, and acceptance criteria. Reproducibility demands every detail that could matter: PCR needs primer sequences, temperatures, and cycle counts, not just 'amplify the DNA'. The best protocols read like code — same inputs, same outputs, any competent lab. This database is the complete protocol: full records with definitions, key facts, procedures, and runnable demo programs, organized on a teaching ladder from Foundations to Advanced.
definition: Experimental Protocol Library: a complete reference database of full protocol records.
key_points: What this database holds: full protocol records, each with definition, key facts, and a runnable demo program.
Scope: A protocol is a complete recipe for an experiment: materials, quantities, conditions, steps, and acceptance criteria.
Every record is the full entry — never a stub or description alone.
Teaching ladder: Foundations first, then Compounded, then Advanced.

Move to Compounded when Foundations feel solid.

t: Core Vocabulary of Experimental Protocol Library
title: Core Vocabulary of Experimental Protocol Library
description: Every field has its own language. These are the working terms of Experimental Protocol Library — learn them first and every later record reads faster: protocol: complete step-by-step procedure for an experiment; control: reference run isolating the variable under test; blinding: hiding group assignments to block bias; calibration: comparing an instrument against a known standard.
definition: The working vocabulary of Experimental Protocol Library: the terms practitioners actually use.
key_points: protocol: complete step-by-step procedure for an experiment
control: reference run isolating the variable under test
blinding: hiding group assignments to block bias
calibration: comparing an instrument against a known standard
replicate: independent repeat of an experiment
standard curve: known-concentration series used to quantify unknowns

Use three terms in a sentence of your own.
